title: ttnn.digamma FLOAT32 is ~4,500 ULP off for x > 102
body:
`ttnn.digamma` supports positive `BFLOAT16` and `FLOAT32` inputs. The
FLOAT32 path is thousands of ULP off for inputs above 102.

## Results

ttsim Blackhole, 4,094 geometrically spaced FLOAT32 inputs in `[102, 3.0e38]`,
`dest_acc=Yes`. Reference: the LLK harness golden, which is `torch.digamma`
evaluated in FLOAT32. I injected `-DINP_FLOAT32`, which TTNN sets for FLOAT32
inputs but the LLK test harness does not.

Since that golden is itself FLOAT32, I checked it against an independent 60-digit
computation: on the points cited below it is bit-exact. This measures the kernel,
not the reference. As a control that the define is in effect, the FLOAT32 branch
measures 1 median ULP on `[0.01, 102]`, where the BFLOAT16 branch measures 48.

| | Current kernel | With fix |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median ULP | 4,543 | 0 |
| p99 ULP | 8,403 | 1 |
| Max ULP | 9,080 | 1 |
| Max relative error | 6.86e-04 | 1.19e-07 |
| Bit-exact results | 1 / 4,094 | 3,930 / 4,094 |

Example:

```
x = 1820.104
reference = 7.50637436
current   = 7.50204468  (9,080 ULP)
fixed     = 7.50637436  (bit-exact)
```

The error is not limited to the largest inputs. Median error is 3,864 ULP on
`[102, 200)`, 5,019 ULP on `[200, 1e3)`, and 4,386 ULP above `1e12`.

## Cause

For `x > 102`, `ckernel_sfpu_digamma.h` uses the Bernoulli asymptotic and calls
`_calculate_log_body_no_init_`. That log body uses:

```
sfpi::vFloat vConstLn2 = 0.692871f;
```

The constant has a `-3.98e-04` relative error. The same body also uses a
third-order mantissa polynomial. At the worst point, the constant accounts for
64% of the error and the polynomial for 36%. Replacing only the constant still
leaves about 176 median ULP in the host model.

The kernel comment says the accurate log body cannot be used because its program
constants conflict with the reciprocal. Calling that body does conflict. The
algorithm itself does not: the same range reduction and FLOAT32 coefficients can
use immediate constants and no program constant registers.

The same branch also returns `89.09284` for `digamma(NaN)`. Its guard handles
infinity but excludes NaN.

## Proposed fix

I have a patch for Blackhole and Wormhole that:

1. uses an immediate-only accurate log body for `INP_FLOAT32`;
2. passes NaN and infinity through;
3. adds TTNN tests for large FLOAT32 inputs, NaN, and infinity.

The `[0.01, 102]` range is bit-identical before and after on both dtypes. The
BFLOAT16 large-x path is unchanged. Static instruction counts for the FLOAT32
path increase by 5.7% on Blackhole and 4.3% on Wormhole. The BFLOAT16 paths
become shorter.

I tested the kernel with ttsim for Blackhole and Wormhole. I do not have
Tenstorrent hardware, so the TTNN device test has not been run.

## Prior work

#51129 changes the same files for the `x < 0.01` recurrence. It does not change
the `x > 102` branch. I rechecked current `main` at `b069c3c794ab`; the two
digamma kernel files are unchanged from my patch base.

Could you please assign this to me?
